transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Ronan.
Democrats have seized the largest House majority since the 1990s.
This after a race calls Sunday for Democrats by the Associated Press in North Carolina.
NPR's Eric McDaniel reports.
The Associated Press says Democrat Chuck Hubbard has ousted Republican incumbent Virginia Fox.
He'll represent the northwest corner of the state near Greensboro.
It's a notable win, not just because Fox was an 83-year-old committee chair who'd been
in Washington more than 20 years, but also because it puts the running tally of Democratic
House seats at 258, matching the high watermark for either party that stretches back to the
1992 election.
And there are still a handful of races left to call.
It could push their majority even higher.
Democrats also have a commanding Senate majority that will need to work with President Trump
to get things signed into law, Eric McDaniel, NPR News in Washington.
In Ukraine near Kiev, a rescue operation is underway after a Russian attack hit an apartment
building killing at least six people.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley has more.
Russia has intensified its drone and missile strikes against Kiev and the surrounding region
as winter approaches.
In the last week, Kiev experienced one of its heaviest assaults of the war after Ukraine
heavily damaged Putin's prized Kerch bridge, which links Russia with the occupied Crimean
Peninsula.
Zelensky has repeatedly urged Ukraine's allies to speed up promised air defense deliveries,
particularly interceptor missiles.
He says in the past week Russia launched 2,700 drones, 1,460 glide bombs, and 165 missiles,
including upgraded North Korean ballistic missiles at 20 Ukrainian regions.
President Trump said he believes Putin is serious about ending the war.
Eleanor Beardsley in PR News, Lviv, Ukraine.
The U.N. Climate Change Conference in Turkey has ended with no agreement among delegates
over ways to combat the growing threat of climate change.
Representatives from European nations and climate-vulnerable nations, including Panama,
rejected a proposed agreement because they said it omitted fossil fuels from the document.
Ireland's environmental minister, Dara O'Brien, blamed the oil industry, along with Russia
and Saudi Arabia.
We regret the fact that we had to take this step, but we could not, with any good conscience,
support a text that effectively denies what is happening in the world and was hijacked
by fossil fuel producers.
The U.S. did not send a delegation to the conference for the second year following the
Trump administration's withdrawal from the Paris Accord.
Authorities in Indonesia say it's too early to determine how many people have died when
a fire swept through a candle factory near the capital of Jakarta.
At least 24 people are dead, but the death toll could go higher as the search continues.
You're listening to NPR News.
Atlanta-based Delta Airline says more than 1,000 flights were delayed Sunday after an
automated system used by flight crews to calculate aircraft weight malfunctioned.
Sunday morning, the FAA issued a one-hour ground stop, this at the airline's main hub
at Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport.
After traveling for more than eight years, a joint European-Japanese mission has gone
into orbit around the planet Mercury.
The probe should provide scientists with a wealth of new information about the innermost
planet in the solar system.
Jalpalka reports.
Mercury is an intriguing planet.
It has an incredible number of scientific mysteries.
Anne Pommier at the Carnegie Institution is one of the scientists on the BepiColombo mission.
She says scientists have found evidence that there is ice at the poles of the planet, odd
for a planet so close to the sun.
It also has a larger metal core than expected.
The fact that this planet is shrinking also is another mystery.
BepiColombo is scheduled to start answering scientific questions next spring.
But first, it will spend several months adjusting its orbit and checking out its instruments.
For NPR News, I'm Joe Palka.
For the first time since 2021, the Big Ten conference does not have a football team in
the top five of the Associated Press top five rankings.
In fact, the highest-rated Big Ten team is UCLA at number 10, a drop of six positions.
The Big Ten's best two teams, UCLA and Indiana, suffered upset losses on Saturday.
is number one, Utah, number two, Notre Dame, third. I'm Dan Roman, NPI.

topics.text: Democrat Chuck Hubbard ousts Republican Virginia Fox in North Carolina House race
Russian drone and missile attack kills at least six in apartment building near Kyiv
UN Climate Change Conference in Turkey ends without agreement over omitting fossil fuels
Fire at candle factory near Jakarta kills at least 24, death toll may rise
Delta Airlines flights delayed after weight-calculation system malfunction; FAA ground stop in Atlanta
Joint European-Japanese BepiColombo probe enters orbit around Mercury
Big Ten has no team in AP top five for first time since 2021 after upset losses
